h: Riverside South London Around Your Visit
p: A quick word on planning: multi-activity venues are at their best when you book your main activities in advance. Pick a couple of highlights for the group, leave time for food and drinks in between, and arrive early so you're not rushing. If you've got younger ones with you, double-check any age or height limits so nobody misses out.

Wandsworth is in a great spot for exploring south-west London. Battersea Power Station, once a derelict landmark and now a busy shopping, dining and leisure destination, is a short trip east, and you can take the lift up one of its famous chimneys for views over the city. Battersea Park, right by the river, has a boating lake, a children's zoo and loads of green space for running around.

Heading the other way, Putney is lovely for a riverside walk, with rowing clubs lining the Thames and plenty of pubs and cafés. The Thames Path runs along much of the riverbank here, so it's easy to string together a long, scenic stroll.

Back in Wandsworth, the old Ram Brewery site has been redeveloped with new shops and places to eat, keeping a nod to the area's brewing heritage. Between the river, the parks and a big night out of games, it's an easy part of London to fill a day.
